# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

**Problem (root, `verifier-inbox.md` 10:02 UTC).** `post/home-movie-2` attributed

were captured up to ~1 s apart while gameplay advanced, and treated them as
simultaneous before/at/after anchor evidence.

**Change.** `shoot()` now delegates to `shootOne()`, which brackets **every**
screenshot with its own cheap pre-shot and post-shot observation
(`sampleProvenance()` — one small read-only `evaluate`, deliberately lighter than
the full sampler so bracketing does not starve the 10 Hz loop). Each frame
records:

- its **own** `provenance.window {startMs, endMs, durationMs}`,
- its **own** `provenance.pre` / `provenance.post` observations,
- its **own** `sha256`, `bytes`, `stats`,
- its **own** `role` — `raw-hud-inclusive` vs `perceptual-hud-suppressed`,
- `provenance.crossings` and `atStateClaimable`.

When `beat / objectiveId / markerLabel / workOrder / anchorId /
activationSequence / milestones` changes while the shutter is open,
`atStateClaimable` is **false** and the frame is reported as lying *inside a
window*. **No exact anchor instant is ever fabricated.**

`pairProvenance()` records `simultaneous: false` unconditionally, the **real**
`pairOffsetMs`, and any state that crossed *between* the two partners.

**Preserved.** Original pixels are written once, hashed, and never re-encoded,
cropped or filtered. HUD suppression remains the shipped `evidence.mjs`
`vox-hide-ui` behaviour, restored in a `finally`. Legacy per-frame

**Boot black frame.** `classifyLuma()` flags a blank frame as
`bootBlackFrameCandidate` and sets `visualAcceptance: false` on **every** frame
without exception. A boot black frame is progression evidence, never visual
acceptance. This harness makes no visible-content claim at all.

=== score-home-anchor
# Score interpretation — home-anchor eligibility

**Later eligible home anchors must remain usable on Continue or a valid deep link while the ineligible live install acknowledgement stays silent.** Suppressing the entire home-anchor sequence is not an interpretation of the signed hydration rule. This is a bounded interpretation of scene-v2, not a new direction, independent runtime acceptance or authorization to fabricate receipts.

Contract: `scene-contract.json`, SHA-256 **`4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`**. Reviewed `verifier-findings.json#VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1`, its home/survey summary artifacts, and the requested source owners.

## Binding clauses

- `/syncAnchors/0` (`anc.cg.cell-installed`) requires the **actual live install receipt**, one consumed cell and at most one acknowledgement when a home score host is available. Its acceptance explicitly says a hydrated entry is steady and silent, consuming no second cell. `/score/cues/0` likewise permits no completion transient on restore and no listening gate.
- `/syncAnchors/1` (`anc.cg.home-steady`) explicitly restores the steady home variant on hydrated entry, without a completion transient or queued acknowledgement. Its real departed/restored receipts, on-foot Tidegarden and actual-core conditions remain required.
- `/guidance/objectives/0` enters at home-steady and states that **a restored save reaches the review objective without replaying the transaction**. Its entry feedback is silent on hydration. The invitation therefore remains functional independently of fresh install presentation.
- `/syncAnchors/2` and `/syncAnchors/3` bind fault-reviewed to the actual core interaction and return-chosen to the explicit F commit. The latter releases the home quotation; fault review does not change it. `/guidance/objectives/1` preserves that voluntary choice. None of these clauses requires another installation.

## Required invariant and evidence distinction

Eligibility, actual activation and audible acknowledgement are distinct. A restored transaction must not be represented as a fresh installation to satisfy ordering. Equally, its ineligible live acknowledgement must not become a permanently pending prerequisite for silent steady entry or subsequent real F actions. Already-earned review/choice state restores without falsely replaying its action; a new eligible interaction retains its signed anchor. No missing receipt, core, actor/world condition or player action may be supplied by this interpretation. Return-chosen still releases home score through the existing authority; travel remains with the world conductor.

The verifier's summaries support an observed separation: the home run reached real review/return progression with an empty home anchor ledger, while the survey run recorded repeated-measure. The home loop stopped at the return-beat predicate at 2777 ms; its later hatch anchor is a separate capture-window issue. Those observations do not justify VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1's conclusion that **all four** home anchors should be observable only during a continuous journey. Only the fresh install event requires that live boundary. The evidence does not itself prove an audible failure: local score dispatch can continue despite rejected AV activation, and no listening occurred here.

Source risk: `noteAnchor` records its local once-latch before calling AV activation and does not consume its returned success value. `activateAnchor` rejects later anchors while an earlier required same-beat anchor remains pending. `enterCommonGroundBeat` requests home-steady on entry, while `tickCommonGroundEntry` calls reactivation before requesting cell-installed. If entry callbacks run before that latter request, the live path can also reject and locally spend home-steady before installation activates. This is an entry-order/latch risk requiring continuous-path evidence, **not an observed continuous-journey failure**.

## Amendment disposition

**No creative contract amendment is required for a bounded eligibility/wiring correction that enforces these existing clauses.** Preserve real event causality, silent restoration, one live install acknowledgement, subsequent actual anchors and existing release behavior. This interpretation prescribes no code and does not waive unrelated anchor ordering, receipt or production-boundary requirements. It neither closes the verifier finding nor establishes implementation success.

Inspected source SHA-256: `commonGroundDirector.ts` `deea059b75dde9bc627ca040a4ccac71d260e0cea9fc3459fe0dd074cce3dec4`; `signedSceneAvRuntime.ts` `01d59a2a44908857fa02e6d9b9849c539a7bbfa74580a7cd724659198e3a9184`. The inspected findings snapshot was `32a46bd46675d78c48546db94e8718dc3fb372cbb928a07df1662272f9fc0283`; the verifier remains active. No source, contract or signature was edited; no new probe, render or listening claim.

=== chapter-manual-corner
# Manual corner interpretation — Chapter

contractVersion: `scene-v2`  
contractSha256: `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`  
contractChangeRequired: **false for a bounded implementation correction meeting the conditions below**  
authoredAt: 2026-09-06T09:47:14.579038+00:00

The signed intent allows ordinary small manual deviations and honest recovery. It requires the real ordered eighteen-unit passage, not frame-perfect coincidence with mathematical corner coordinates. It does not bind `routeProgressUnits`' current projection algorithm or promise credit for omitted ground. A deviation may leave part of the route unproved; the player must be able to resume its actual traversal through ordinary movement, without a hidden precision ritual, reset, additional F or new corner prompts.

This is an interpretation of source and recorded engineering evidence, **not an independently observed manual failure**. `producer-manual-corner-risk.json` records the director test turning at z15.82 before z16 and stalling at four credited units; it also records the corrected movie controller completing its actual eighteen-unit test. Browser/manual acceptance remains pending. In `main/src/story/commonGroundRoute.ts:444–479`, each accepted arc projection must fit `previousUnits + displacementUnits` for that frame; later projections can stay beyond that ceiling after an early turn. The source supports the reported risk but does not establish its frequency or the usability of recovery in play.

The relevant exact signed clauses are:

- `scene-contract.json#/guidance/objectives/13/acceptanceCriterion`: full actual eighteen-unit E→C passage, and first-time manual success without private route knowledge, a rail or per-corner prompts.
- `#/story/agencyWindows/3/mandatoryPath`: the complete guided common route and both real reciprocal traversals; positioning earns no proof. Its `fallbackSemantics` requires a safe hold and actionable objective when a predicate is unmet, while `rescueSemantics` forbids granting progress to escape a stall.
- `#/story/events/21/acceptanceCriterion`: current H reference, solid sight, grounding and clearance throughout; endpoint separation, old footsteps, saved proof and elapsed time cannot substitute. The matching `#/syncAnchors/21/acceptanceCriterion` binds the same event.

If independent verification confirms the risk, a bounded correction must let genuinely performed ordered traversal resume from retained valid progress and reach actual C while still proving the **full actual eighteen units**, maintained reference, supported movement, body clearance and physical arrival. It must neither discard earned progress because of a small steering error nor credit the missing portion merely because the body reached a later segment. Stationary time, looping elsewhere, endpoint proximity, skipped bends, accumulated unrelated distance and automatic rescue remain insufficient. Restore must preserve earned facts and revalidate current physical conditions.

That outcome implements existing v2 agency and proof requirements; it needs no contract amendment. A proposal that shortens the passage, skips order or physical checks, changes route geometry, adds a required input/target, or manufactures credit would exceed this interpretation and require separate routing. No algorithm, tolerance, source patch or new repair authorization is prescribed here. Root retains repair routing; independent manual and Continue proof remains necessary even though the movie test passes.

# Common Ground (ch13) — independent verification, INTERIM FAILURE CHECKPOINT

**This is not chapter verification.** It is not a scorecard, not acceptance and
not a publication decision. Machine-readable twin with every file hash:
`verification-world-interim-report.json`. Findings: `verifier-findings.json`.
Phase log: `verifier-progress.md`.

Written under root control `pause` (11:42:15Z), whose instruction is to
finalize, record, and end the invocation cleanly. That is the current state —
the earlier 11:32 pause is superseded and nothing is waiting.

## Verdict

**FAIL (interim).** The lifecycle repair genuinely fixed both blockers measured
on the previous source, and the chapter now reaches and *accepts* its first real
anchors on hardware. Two **new** blocking runtime defects stop it before a
single route sample is recorded, and the valid intermediate-Continue case root
asked for is still unproved — because the physical prerequisite for it cannot be
earned while blocker 1 stands.

## Identity — what was measured, on what

| | |
| --- | --- |
| contract | scene-v2 `4dbf722b…ff88e` |
| source manifest | `51b25376…02c3` — control, readiness and the manifest file all agree |
| independent source rehash | **96/96 identical, 0 missing**, re-checked again after the build |
| static gate | `npm --prefix main run verify` → **EXIT 0, 348 files, 3068 tests, build ok**, 61 s |
| preview | root-owned `http://127.0.0.1:45091/`, root exec session 89502 |
| identity recheck | `<title>Paravoxia</title>`; index **and** bundle `index-Bquz6XRz.js` are **byte-identical to my own build's `main/dist`**; the served bytes contain the new `__paravoxiaCommonGround` hook and the exact signed marker strings |
| renderer | ANGLE (NVIDIA GB10/PCIe, OpenGL 4.5.0) — **hardware, headed**, heavy lock taken with `flock -n` and released |

I started no server and own none. The old 43617 preview is stopped and no claim
here comes from it.

**The static gate is permission to measure, not acceptance.** Both blockers
below are invisible to all 3068 tests.

## What the repair actually fixed (measured, not read)

- **`?story=ch13-survey` now boots ON FOOT.** The rail walked the body ~60 units
  to the survey start and performed the shipped F resolver. No disembark
  fixture, no teleport, no grant.
- **The capsule-centre frame is reconciled.** The published diagnostic reports
  `bodyCentre` 52.7890 and grounded `bodyPose` 50.9890 — exactly 1.8 apart along
  the *live* up — and the body arrives 0.303 horizontal units from the authored
  S, inside the 0.35 arrive radius.
- **Signed anchors are being accepted again.** `anc.cg.repeated-measure` and
  `anc.cg.demonstration-opened` activated in order (sequence 1, 2), and
  `anc.cg.hatch-boarded` / `anc.cg.lift-committed` on `ch13-return`.
- **`ch13-home` plays**: review entered at 11 ms with the exact signed label and
  work order, performed through the shared resolver, choose-return followed, and
  the beat advanced at 2704 ms with 0 nudges and 0 page errors.

## Blocker 1 — VF3-FOOTING-1: the footing query and the body disagree by exactly one voxel cell

At S the shipped F resolver was performed **200 times**
(`story-ch13-survey-start`, `source: resolver-perform`, `performOutcome:
returned` every time). `survey.phase` never left `awaiting-start`, **zero**
samples were recorded, and the prompt stayed live with no explanation. The
chapter's own diagnostic reported `supported: false` in **1501 of 1555**
world-bound samples. The only other gate is `CG_POINT_REACH 2.0`, satisfied at
0.310.

A bounded diagnostic then measured *why*, using nothing but the published
diagnostic and the **shipped Space jump**, sampling `supported` as a function of
the body's own height at the audit site:

| voxel cell `cy` | feet y range | samples | supported = true |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 25 (the cell the body stands on) | 50.989 – 51.908 | 13 | **0** |
| 26 (one cell up) | 52.123 – 54.047 | 59 | **59** |
| 27 | 54.083 – 54.212 | 14 | **0** |

`cy = round((feetY − 1.05) / 2)`, `VOXEL_SCALE = 2`; cell *k* spans world y
`[2k−1, 2k+1)`. A lift into cell 26 returning **true** requires `solid(26)` AND
`air(27)`. So the terrain model the footing query reads believes the ground's
top face at the audit site is **y = 53**, while the body physically stands with
its feet at **y = 50.99** — one whole voxel cell, 2 world units, lower. The
authored ch13 poses (51.05) match the **physical** surface, not the queried
model. At the landing area the two agree (standing feet 51.16–51.30, cell 25,
supported **true**), so the disagreement is **localised, not global**.

What is still inferred: an outside observer cannot separate "solid(25) is false"
from "solid(26) blocks the cell-above test", and cannot tell whether the gap
comes from `voxelSystem.hasVoxel` vs `generator.shouldVoxelExist`, from a
WorldSave/`isDeleted` gap, or from an audit-site clearing that exists in the
collider/render but not in the generator. **No cause is asserted, no rounding
claim is made** (`Math.round` maps both 50.989 and the authored 51.05 to the
same cell 25), and **no predicate, radius or tolerance was touched**.

For the engineer's reproduction, the world identity is legible in the captured
HUD frame: **seed 3215739679, world coordinate −1,−1, 125,000 voxels**.

**The player-facing shape of this defect** (raw HUD frame
`0034-strip-ch13-survey.png`): the exact signed marker *"Survey start · begin a
route"*, the correct standing work order, the live `F | Begin recording your
route` prompt, and a marker distance of **0 m** — while the verb does nothing,
200 times, silently. The guidance is right and the world refuses it.

## Blocker 2 — VF3-AVHOME-1: the ch13-home anchors are noted but never accepted by the AV rail

Through the whole of `ch13-home` the signed AV runtime reported `beat:
ch13-home`, `activationSequence: 0`, `activationHistoryAnchorIds: []` and an
**empty** pending queue, while the chapter's diagnostic listed
`firedAnchors ['anc.cg.home-steady','anc.cg.fault-reviewed']`. The AV ledger
only begins at `anc.cg.hatch-boarded`, in the next beat.

Source candidates, cited not asserted: `anc.cg.home-steady` is neither
conditional nor present in `RECEIPT_SATISFIED_ANCHORS`, so once its own
activation is lost, `signedSceneAvRuntime.ts:536-545` refuses every later
`ch13-home` anchor behind it — a cascade from one lost anchor. The single retry
in `drainPendingAnchors` (`commonGroundDirector.ts:461-470`) runs at the *top* of
the tick, and `clearPendingAnchors` empties the queue at the beat entry itself.
An initial foreground/visibility cancel at boot is a further **untested**
candidate.

**Precision, per root:** `noteAnchor` drives this chapter's mood/music
separately from AV acceptance, and root observed `score.mood = restored-home`.
This finding therefore claims only that **the signed AV rail did not accept the
anchors** (no activation history, no shot/lens). It makes **no** claim that a cue
was inaudible or that chapter music failed. **Nothing was listened to.**

Scope limit: measured on a **deep link**. The continuous station → home entry
has not been run on this source.

## Still-open proof gap — the valid intermediate Continue (CG008)

What exists is an **isolated AV-order boundary probe** on the real runtime
(direct anchor calls, no WorldSave reconstruction): with no ch13 receipt held,
`anc.cg.route-offered` and `anc.cg.route-tested` are refused; with
`story:ch13-route-tested` held they succeed. The whole source declares only
**six** durable ch13 milestones, and `RECEIPT_SATISFIED_ANCHORS` keys every
survey predecessor on the **final** one, so a save taken mid-drawing can carry
nothing that excuses them. Root's correction is accepted and the invented
milestone strings were removed.

**The mid-common case does not reproduce**: the crossing receipt is marked
before its anchor is noted, and it excuses `anc.cg.reciprocal-reference`.

This is **not** the valid physical Continue that was asked for. It could not be
produced, because blocker 1 refuses the very first survey sample. The bounded
engineer pass must reproduce it through the real save/driver seam.

## Harness defects found — in MY probes, fixed in MY probes

No game source and no game test file was added, changed or deleted.

1. **The stall predicate never armed** for the entire 189.8 s survey run: its
   phase came from `__autopilot.routeAction`, which reports `idle` throughout
   this chapter's screening rail — 200 consecutive `phase-out-of-scope:idle`
   resets. It now leads with the chapter's own executed rail action.
2. **`cgHoldReason` read a flat key**; the published schema nests it under
   `.diagnostic`, so a real hold never extended the window.
3. **Pose selection now leads with the published hook**, and a change of pose
   *source* is recorded as a measurement discontinuity rather than counted as a
   teleport — the earlier run's 54.77-unit "largest jump" was the boot
   placeholder switching to the real hook.
4. The new footing probe awaited the **synchronous** `frameStats` helper and
   crashed at its final write; fixed, and its summary is reconstructed offline
   from its own trace and labelled as such. Every measurement in it is verbatim
   from the live run.

Offline: `cg-harness-selftest` **25/25** (was 23/23), `--self-test` OK,
`node --check` OK. These are harness checks, **not game proof**.

## Not measured, not claimed

No route sample, neither route class, no ordered 18 units, no corner behaviour,
no manual-corner recovery, no common beat, no completion or handback; no three
cold journeys, no station→home bridge, no full story movie; the 28 anchors as a
set, the 17+2 objective lifecycles end to end, the reset matrix and the
mobile / reduced-motion / lowest-tier variants are all untouched; every
performance figure is unmeasured; and **nothing was listened to**. None of these
is recorded as passed anywhere.

## Integrity

No game source modified. No threshold, predicate, radius or tolerance touched.
No teleport, progress grant, prerequisite fixture or timeout rescue used or
counted as success. No server started by this role and none orphaned; the
root-owned preview at `http://127.0.0.1:45091/` is root's and is untouched by
this role's exit. All prior captures, logs and reports are preserved.

**A failed interim checkpoint is not chapter verification complete.** Independent
re-verification of the repaired source, and the mandatory post-fix physical
journeys, all remain required. No publication is authorized.
